jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in SNSPDs
jobs.description:
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) is expanding its talented and international team to add to its cutting-edge quantum programme in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, we are running an international quantum computing programme, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, that drives research and innovations at multiple levels - from developing scalable quantum processor technologies to quantum algorithms and applications.  The long-term mission of the programme is to develop fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve life-science-relevant chemical and biological problems.

  The project 
 The position is centred on the development of integrated superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) embedded in controllable photonic circuits for the fully integrated processing of the emitted photons from silicon quantum emitters. The work will be performed as part of the Photonic Control and Readout team in NQCP, in close collaboration with the Theory & Simulation and the Materials engineering teams at NQCP and the Growth team at Quantum Foundry. These teams will support the efforts of the development and integration of SNSPDs in our photonic circuit.

  You will be collaborating closely with the other team members of the Photonic C&R team and – like the rest of the team - be generally involved in the projects related to the platform. A number of students will also be dedicated to the SNSPD projects. The nanofabrication is done at the DTU Nanolab – a 1,350 m² ISO 4–6 cleanroom with over 150 state-of-the-art tools, and one of the leading cleanrooms in Europe. Testing and integration of the SNSPDs will be done at the NQCP Photonics lab at the Niels Bohr Institute established in 2023. The lab contains a range of cryostats (mK to 4K) designed for optical fibre access, state-of-the-art electronics, commercial SNSPDs, etc.

  Responsibilities:

   	
• Taking the leading role in developing and integrating SNSPDs into our photonic circuits and establishing the electrical control circuit. 	
• Structuring the efforts on multiple projects, integrating experimental results in our database, and providing feedback to collaborating teams. 	
• Contributing to the other projects within the Photonics team. The projects span single photon sources and optical components like switches, cavities, etc. 	
• Teaching and supervision of students. 	
• Procurement, maintenance, and operation of scientific equipment.    

  We are looking for the following qualifications: 

   	
• PhD with postdoc experience in experimental physics, engineering, nanotechnologies, or related. 	
• Experience with SNSPDs fabrication and characterisation, quantum photonics, electronics, and cryogenic systems. 	
• Experience with control software and data logging – preferably in python. 	
• Good communication skills and a structured approach to work.   
 Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory but documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered.
 
 The position is also open as a postdoc. Please apply to the call corresponding to the position relevant for you. Only one of the positions will be filled.

  
 General criteria apply to the appointment of Assistant Professors at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, Innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

  For Assistant professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5a_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-Assistant_professors.pdf.
 
 Why Us? 
 Joining NQCP now, you will get involved in a well-established and ambitious programme, which offers excellent opportunites to build a career in advancing quantum computing. We want to make Denmark a world leader in quantum research, and we hope to attract people from all over the world.  

  Life in Denmark is supported with strong social services (free universal healthcare, free/subsidised language courses, paid parental leave, subsidised day care institutions and excellent public schools). Our work culture is very egalitarian and prioritises work life balance. Dual career families are the norm, and workplaces offer flexibility to support everyone in having both an exciting career and good family time. Danish cities are known for having excellent infrastructure, for example through widespread bike path networks. We can also offer a thriving food-scene, excellent museums, and beautiful natural scenery. 
 
 Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen's Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact here.
  

  Further information on the Department can be found on the Niels Bohr Institute website. Inquiries about the position can be made to Stefano Paesani: stefano.paesani@nbi.ku.dk or Peter Granum: peter.granum@nbi.ku.dk.

   

  Start date is the 1st of February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
 
 The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment
 The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

   

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

   

  Please include

  2.                         Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 

  3.                         Original PhD diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish.

  4.                         Publication list

  5.                         Reference letters
  

  The deadline for applications is 1st of December 2026 23:59 GMT +1. 

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee.

Our Europe Central Inhouse Consulting team is growing, and we are looking for an experienced Manager or Assistant Director to join us in Copenhagen.

We act as an internal consulting partner to EY leadership, Functions and Service Lines across 33 countries in Europe Central, helping solve complex business challenges, translate strategic priorities into practical solutions and deliver change with lasting impact.

Reporting to the Europe Central Inhouse Consulting Lead, you will lead and contribute to high-priority projects across countries, functions and organizational boundaries. Assignments may range from strategy and operating model design to transformation, implementation and business improvement.

We are a small, collaborative team with a hands-on, pragmatic approach. We value constructive problem-solvers who take ownership, create momentum and turn ideas into results.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in plant-microbe interactions
jobs.description:
Postdoc in plant-microbe interactions at AU Flakkebjerg Aarhus University
The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, is offering a postdoctoral position in plant-biofertilizer interactions, starting 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position will be available for a 24-month period.

You will be part of a research environment focusing on plant-microbe interactions. You will be contributing to specifically the area of how different cereal genotypes interact with soil microbiomes and biofertilizers, and the focus of your position will be to study i) root colonization efficiency of biologicals on a range of cereal lines and ii) the effect of cereal cultivar mixtures on root microbiomes.

We expect that you will be an important part of the research environment and that you will contribute positively to the social working environment. We also expect that you will take part in our teaching activities and that you will report research results in high-impact scientific journals.

Your profile
We are searching for a highly motivated candidate who has:

• A PhD in plant-microbe interactions or similar
• Collaborative skills and ability to demonstrate commitment in teams. A fondness of taking the initiative and the motivation to pursue a scientific career
• Documented experience in scientific writing and publication in peer-reviewed scientific journals
• Research experience in areas of microbial ecology and plant biology
Additional qualifications
Further, we will prefer candidates with some of the following qualifications:

• Teaching and supervision experience at the BSc and MSc level
• Interest and experience in developing competitive national and international research applications
• Experience in planning and conducting laboratory work within plants, microbiology and greenhouse experiments
• Insight into plant physiology and nutrition
• Experience with high-throughput sequencing (metabarcoding and RNASeq) and advanced microscopy
Who we are
At the Department of Agroecology, our main goal is to contribute to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. The department consists of nine research sections with around 350 highly skilled employees, of which approximately 50% are scientific staff. More information can be found here.

We believe in encouraging inclusion, acceptance, and understanding by employing staff who bring unique perspectives to our department.

What we offer
• A collaborative, international research environment that combines high academic standards with an informal and supportive atmosphere. We value accountability, curiosity, flexibility, and teamwork in everything we do.
• An inclusive and respectful workplace culture, where mutual trust, kindness, and professional dialogue are part of daily life. We encourage open communication and develop a cohesive sense of community across teams and disciplines.
• A flexible working environment that supports work-life balance and individual needs.
• An active institutional commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion – in recruitment, career development, and everyday interactions.
• An innovative and meaningful workplace where your work contributes to solving real-world challenges. No two days are alike, and we welcome creative thinking and new ideas.
• Support for international researchers and their families, including Relocation Service and an Expat Partner Programme
Living and working in Denmark
• Subsidised childcare and free education from primary school through university.
• Universal healthcare for you and your family as residents.
• Five weeks of paid holiday per year.
• Generous parental leave – up to 52 weeks shared between parents, with full or partial salary.
Place of Work
The place of work is Aarhus University, Campus Flakkebjerg. The affiliation will be with the Department of Agroecology.

Contact information 
For further information about the position, please contact Mogens Nicolaisen at mn@agro.au.dk.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. jobs.occupation: Senior Director, Injectables Quality Denmark
jobs.description:
Senior Director, Injectables Quality Denmark

Your impact begins here

As Senior Director, Injectables Quality Denmark, you will lead Quality across four Danish sites and rethink how Quality works alongside manufacturing. You will bring leaders together, challenge established ways of working and drive simplification, productivity and innovation through technology, AI and new operating models. All while ensuring patient safety, compliance and reliable supply. Your impact will show in stronger collaboration across Hillerød, Gentofte, Bagsværd and Kalundborg, and in building a high-performing Quality organisation where colleagues feel empowered to challenge, improve and drive change.

What you’ll bring

You are a senior leader with pharmaceutical industry experience, who has led change in complex environments, who earns trust across sites and functions, and who has brought people with you through periods of transformation.

• Substantial experience from the pharmaceutical industry, with a strong background in quality (QA or QC), in manufacturing, or a combination of both, and strong GMP expertise.

• Proven experience as a leader of leader, preferably across more than one site, with responsibility for talent development, succession planning, budgets and organisational performance.

• A strong track record of driving transformation and operational improvements, including productivity gains, inspections and Quality support for new products or expansions.

• Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders across functions and countries, including digitalisation, automation or changes to operating models.

• Leadership that builds trust and psychological safety, and the courage to set a clear direction when change is challenging.

• Sound judgement in critical Quality decisions, balancing compliance and business needs without compromising patient safety.

What you’ll do

You will lead the Danish Injectables Quality organisation through a period of transformation, with the ambition of making Quality a stronger enabler of manufacturing performance and a competitive advantage for Novo. Lead Quality across four sites, ensuring robust GMP compliance, inspection readiness and effective quality risk management.

• Challenge existing processes, remove complexity and use technology, AI and smarter ways of working to deliver measurable productivity improvements, rather than adding headcount whenever volumes rise.

• Build one leadership team across the sites. Coach, challenge and develop leaders, set clear accountability and strengthen succession and talent pipelines.

• Help colleagues see ongoing change as progress. Set a clear direction and keep teams healthy and engaged while the way of working evolves.

• Strengthen collaboration and leverage capabilities across sites, and help shape shared set-ups across sites.

• Ensure Quality readiness for new products, capacity expansions and production ramp-up, and act as a trusted partner to manufacturing leadership.

• Take an active seat in the Drug Product Manufacturing Quality leadership team, helping shape priorities across the wider Quality organisation as well as your own area.

Who you’ll work with

You will report to the VP, Drug Product Manufacturing Quality and be part of the Drug Product Manufacturing Quality leadership team, contributing to the strategic direction and transformation of Quality across our international drug product manufacturing network.

You will lead an experienced leadership team responsible for an organisation of more than 240 colleagues, including specialists and Qualified Persons. You will support the Qualified Persons while respecting their independent responsibility for batch certification and release.

Your closest partners will be site and manufacturing leaders across Hillerød, Gentofte, Bagsværd and Kalundborg, alongside MSAT, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, Digital and IT, P&O and Finance. You will also work with health authorities, inspectors, auditors, suppliers and technology partners. You will be expected to put collective success ahead of local optimisation and to speak up early when things stall.

What you can expect here

You will have real scope to shape how Quality works at Novo. You will be trusted to make decisions, challenge the status quo and take ownership, with clear expectations for performance and honest feedback in both directions.

You will grow through a broad leadership remit across four sites, close collaboration with the Drug Product Manufacturing Quality leadership team, as well as the Drug Product Manufacturing Denmark Injectables leadership team and the chance to influence priorities beyond your own area. You will work at the forefront of digitalisation, automation and AI in Quality, with a team that values curiosity and decisive action.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead Quality through change, bring four sites closer together and show how Quality can make manufacturing faster and simpler, apply for the role by December 6.

jobs.occupation: Tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor Functional Biology and Ecology of Marine Animals
jobs.description:
Department of Biology, Faculty of Science
 University of Copenhagen, Denmark

  The Department of Biology at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a position as Tenure-track or Associate Professor in functional biology and ecology of marine animals. The position is set to be filled by June 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter, pending negotiation.

  Position Overview
 We are looking for a passionate, innovative and collaborative researcher with expertise in hypothesis driven research on the functional biology and experimental ecology of marine animals. The ideal candidate will complement and strengthen our existing research areas, and take advantage of our experimental facilities and easy access to different coastal ecosystems. We expect the successful candidate to take a leading role in establishing an externally funded research program and take an active part in developing existing and new courses in the teaching curriculum of the section.

  Key responsibilities include:

   	
• Leading research initiatives and securing third-party funding 	
• Teaching and supervising students at undergraduate, graduate, and PhD levels, with primary teaching responsibilities in the biology degree program 	
• Disseminating research and scientific results to the public 	
• Participating in departmental committees and other tasks as requested   The Research Environment
 The candidate will join the Section for Marine Biology, which operates across both the Copenhagen and Helsingør campuses. The position will be based in Helsingør, where laboratory and office facilities will be provided. The section’s research encompasses a wide range of topics within marine biology including aquatic microbiology and virology, sensory biology, physiology and functional biology of marine organisms, climate change biology, aquaculture, coral reef biology, deep sea biology and the diversity, phylogeny, and evolution of metazoans and protists. Studies are conducted across polar, temperate, and (sub)tropical ecosystems.

  The section boasts modern laboratories equipped with state-of-the-art tools and infrastructure for experimental research including sea-water facilities for animal keeping. This also includes specialized labs for microenvironmental analyses, respirometry, electrophysiology, advanced bioimaging, and DNA and RNA analyses. Additionally, our research vessel, Ophelia, and the proximity to diverse marine habitats in Øresund and other areas provide an excellent platform for a broad range of biological studies.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Sufficiency-based Building Design and Energy System Optimisation
jobs.description:
Are you interested in understanding how the concept of sufficiency affects the optimal design of buildings and their energy systems, and can you contribute to the development of the CEBE programme? Then the Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering invites you to apply for a 2-year postdoc position.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2–year position from 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible. This is a fixed-term position to end on 28 February 2029.

Job description
We are offering a Postdoctoral research position in Building Design and Energy System Optimisation, with particular focus on:

• Optimization-oriented modelling of buildings and their energy system.
• Formulation of optimization frameworks, and integration of multidisciplinary aspects.
• Cross-domain collaboration with social science, on the concept of sufficiency in buildings.
This position is part of the larger CEBE research program, within Research Field 6 - Sufficiency, well-being and energy efficiency. The research tasks will be carried out in a collaborative setting, at Aarhus University with Michael Dahl Knudsen, and with continuous cooperation with RF6 researchers from AAU, DTU, and SDU.

Your profile
The ideal candidate has:

• A PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Civil Engineering, or similar.
• Strong background in one or more of the following areas: Building physics, occupant behaviour modelling, energy systems modelling, numerical optimization methods.
• Documented experience in handling research challenges
• Solid programming skills (e.g. Python, Matlab)
• Interest in interdisciplinary work involving social science
• Strong written and verbal English communication skills
Who we are
The Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering at Aarhus University is a growing engineering environment with a clear vision for the future of the built environment.

Established in 2021, the department today includes more than 100 researchers and educators and around 1.050 students.

We conduct research and education within structural engineering, geotechnics, architectural engineering and design, sustainability, construction management, climate adaptation, indoor climate, building materials, and digital technologies.

The construction sector is facing major challenges related to climate, resource consumption, and the way we design and build our cities and buildings.

Through research, education, and collaboration with industry and public sector partners, we contribute to developing technological solutions that support a more sustainable built environment.

Our research and development activities are closely connected to the needs of industry and society, and many projects are carried out in collaboration with companies, public authorities, and other research environments. This ensures that the knowledge and technologies developed at the department are relevant in practice and create value beyond the university.

Education is a central part of the department’s identity. We offer Bachelor’s, Master’s, and PhD programmes in engineering and continuously work to improve the connection between research, teaching, and practice.

Across our programmes, students work with real-world challenges, current technologies, and sustainable solutions for the construction sector.

What we offer
We offer an innovative and collaborative teaching and research environment with close interaction between students, researchers, and industry partners.

The department provides well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories, and access to shared technical facilities.

We offer an interdisciplinary environment with national, international, and industrial collaborators.

Our academic environment is built on collaboration, knowledge sharing, and professional dialogue.

The workplace is characterised by professionalism, flexibility, and a healthy work–life balance.

The department is located at Navitas on the waterfront in Aarhus, Denmark

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, Navitas, 8000 Aarhus C, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Associate Professor, Massimo Fiorentini, +45 9352 2961, massimo@cae.au.dk

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 14 December 2026.

Shortlisting is used. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in applied microbial dynamics for tropical farm fermentations - BRIGHT
jobs.description:
Are you interested in microbial ecology and food fermentation, and at the same time eager to work towards more sustainable food systems? Then join us as our new PhD Student in tropical farm fermentations

The overwhelming majority of coffee and cocoa are produced in the tropics, and represent vast economic drivers globally as these products continue to transform from commodities to luxury goods. Alongside other factors, the quality of these goods is largely influenced by post-harvest processing, which modulates microbial activity, in turn leading to differences in sensory impact. Complex microbial dynamics affect fermentation outcomes and sensory attributes, and understanding these dynamics and how relevant microbial consortia can be mobilised to modulate these outcomes pose challenging questions that can lead to multiple applications, including ones with health implications. This project aims to unravel some of the underlying microbial dynamics of tropical fermentations such as coffee, cocoa, or other traditional tropical fermentation, utilizing a combination of metagenomics, strain characterization, and solid-state fermentation.

This position is part of a wider cross-institutional research programme on “Microbial fermentation innovations for a resilient food system, optimised human health and environmental sustainability”. You will be working at the interface of biotechnology, genetics, and fermentation in a cutting-edge interdisciplinary and multi-cultural research environment, and will have the opportunity to go on research stay (one-year minimum, preferably two) with our partner institution the Biotransformation & Engineering (BTE) department at the Singapore Institute of Food and Biotechnology Innovation (SIFBI) under the Agency for Science, Research and Technology (A*STAR) in Singapore.

The job
As our PhD student in tropical farm fermentations, you will:

• Analyse metagenomic profiles of artisanal tropical fermentations
• Characterise extant yeast and bacteria for relevant traits for fermentative capability and other functional capacities
• Perform solid state fermentations in controlled settings to achieve targeted outcomes
• Evaluate fermentations via microbiology, molecular biology, and analytic chemistry
• Validate effects of post-fermentation processing on physicochemical qualities and aroma profiles
• Explore potential environmental and socio-economic ramifications of luxury commodities from tropical farm fermentations
What we’re looking for
You will have a two-year Master’s degree (120 ECTS points) in molecular biology, genetics, biotechnology, microbiology, or closely related disciplines, or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year Master's degree.

You will have excellent organizational and project management skills and enjoy developing new methods.

You will be fluent in spoken and written English and have literacy in common IT systems

The ideal candidate will also:

• have experience with molecular biology techniques and, ideally, some foundational understanding in metagenomics, microbial ecology, microbiology, analytical chemistry and/or sensory science
• have a genuine interest in food systems and sustainability
• be able to work with others and independently, and adaptable to working in multi-cultural environments
• be comfortable in an interdisciplinary environment, and a willingness to bridge microbial biotechnology with food and sensory science
• be patient, charitable, curious and playful—key qualities for interdisciplinary work
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by co-supervisors, Dr. Tiffany Mak and Dr. Eric Peterson, and primary supervisor, Prof. Morten Sommer.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years, full time. 

Start date is 01-04-2027 or according to mutual agreement. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
For additional information about the position, please contact Researcher Tiffany Mak at tifmak@dtu.dk, or Senor Scientist Eric Peterson at Eric_Peterson@a-star.edu.sg. 

You can read more about BRIGHT below, and at www.bright.dtu.dk 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 15 December 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• One letter of reference, with referee’s email and phone number
Candidates will be invited to the first round of interviews between 7-11 January 2027.

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

Microbial Foods Group
The Microbial Foods Group is focused on exploring fundamental microbial processes within our food system from a planetary health perspective. We are committed to addressing pressing global food systems and sustainability challenges through integrated and multi-scalar approaches. A key goal is to understand and develop microbially-driven processes that can be effectively implemented to substantially reduce the environmental impact of our current food production system.

BRIGHT – The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRIGHT) is a major initiative based at DTU that aims to accelerate the development of biosolutions and strengthen the bio-based economy. BRIGHT serves as a hub for academic and industrial partners working together to unlock the potential of bioproduction. BRIGHT focuses on three main areas: Sustainable materials (Developing bio-based alternatives to fossil-derived materials), Microbial foods (Innovating food production through microbial technologies), and Microorganisms for net-zero agriculture (Creating solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in agriculture). The goal is to develop and scale innovative biosolutions within these areas, ultimately creating sustainable and competitive alternatives to fossil-based products and processes that can make significant contributions to reducing global greenhouse gas emissions.

Biotransformation & Engineering (BTE)
The Biotransformation & Engineering division brings together the complementary expertise of Biotransformation and Strain Engineering to form a dynamic and synergistic hub for sustainable innovation. By seamlessly integrating advanced biotransformation technologies with precision strain engineering, we drive the creation of high-value compounds, including nutraceuticals, flavors, personal care ingredients, and functional bioactives. As a unified force of innovation and sustainability, the division combines strengths in biocatalysis, fermentation, strain engineering, and synthetic biology to pioneer science-driven solutions that are shaping the future of food and consumer care industries.

Singapore Institute of Food and Biotechnology Innovation (SIFBI)
The A*STAR Singapore Institute of Food and Biotechnology Innovation brings together biotechnology, food and sensory science, nutrition and digestive health to create sustainable ingredients and consumer-driven health solutions for Asia. From discovery and biomanufacturing to product design and human validation, we help partners translate science into meaningful outcomes for people, industry and Singapore.

Agency for Science, Research and Technology (A*STAR)
The Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) is Singapore's lead public sector R&D agency. Through open innovation, we collaborate with our partners in both the public and private sectors to benefit the economy and society. As a Science and Technology Organisation, A*STAR bridges the gap between academia and industry. Our research creates economic growth and jobs for Singapore, and enhances lives by improving societal outcomes in healthcare, urban living, and sustainability. A*STAR plays a key role in nurturing scientific talent and leaders for the wider research community and industry. A*STAR's R&D activities span biomedical sciences to physical sciences and engineering, with research entities primarily located in Biopolis and Fusionopolis.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in microbial lipid fermentation - BRIGHT
jobs.description:
Are you interested in microbial fermentation and metabolism, and at the same time eager to work towards more sustainable food systems? Then join us as our new PhD Student in microbial lipid fermentation! 

Global food processing generates large volumes of high-fat food industry sidestreams (e.g.,

spent coffee grounds, cereal bran, oilseed press cakes, waste cooking oils) that are underutilised, variable in composition and often relegated to low-value uses or waste management. This project addresses three interlinked challenges that block circular valorisation for food: (i) feedstock heterogeneity and food-safety constraints that prevent predictable bioprocessing; (ii) poor fermentability and undesirable sensory compounds (e.g., caffeine, polyphenols, off odours) that inhibit microbial conversion; and (iii) the lack of robust, food-grade microbial platforms capable of growing and producing tailored lipids on real waste streams. 

Focusing on high-fat sidestreams in both Denmark and Singapore, this project has two key aims: 1) to systematically characterise and develop suitable food-grade pretreatments e.g. selective extraction, targeted fermentation etc., to improve nutrition, sensory quality and fermentability of selected sidestreams, and 2) to adapt oleaginous yeasts for high tolerance, growth and lipid production on oils and fats in place of sugars as feedstock, and to optimise fermentation conditions for high titre production of microbial lipids. Taking a multi-omics approach that includes genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics and lipidomics, this project seeks to establish an in-depth understanding of the bioprocess, derisking further scale-up while demonstrating pathways to sustainable, high-value food ingredients and co-products.

This position is part of a wider cross-institutional research programme on “Microbial fermentation innovations for a resilient food system, optimised human health and environmental sustainability”. You will be working at the interface of biotechnology, genetics, and fermentation in a cutting-edge interdisciplinary and multi-cultural research environment, and will have the opportunity to go on research stay (one-year minimum) with our partner institution the Biotransformation & Engineering (BTE) department at the Singapore Institute of Food and Biotechnology Innovation (SIFBI) under the Agency for Science, Research and Technology (A*STAR) in Singapore.

Existing microbial food productions have largely focused on liquid state fermentation as the main production strategy under industrial settings. This approach however limits the media composition, excluding the potential use of substrates with lower solubility, as well as substrates mixtures that are heterogeneous by nature. Are you passionate about data analytics, optimization, transport, and environment? Do you want to work on a research project that has a concrete impact on society? 

We invite you to apply for a full-time PhD position at DTU Management (Department of Technology, Management, and Economics) as part of an international Alliance PhD collaboration between DTU Management and Télécom SudParis, Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IPP), France. The project “ASTRA” (Analytics for Spatio-Temporal Regional trAnsport models) explores how emerging data sources can be better integrated into demand estimation, and aims to develop a working prototype for the national Danish transport model.

Knowing how many people travel, where and when is the foundation of every transport model, and ultimately of decisions on infrastructure investments, transport policy and the green transition. Yet estimating mobility demand for large networks remains one of the main bottlenecks in transport modelling. The problem is highly non-linear, underdetermined and difficult to solve for large-scale networks, and existing methods often rely on proprietary, non-reproducible data and an oversimplified representation of travel behaviour. As a result, they often fail to represent travel decisions realistically, which can lead to misallocated infrastructure and ineffective policy interventions. At the same time, new data sources are emerging. Mobile networks, and in particular 5G antennas, continuously capture anonymous mobility traces, while travel surveys provide rich behavioural and socio-economic information, but only for small samples, and are rarely used in demand estimation.

The ASTRA project will develop a demand estimation framework that combines high-resolution behavioural data, such as the Danish National Travel Survey, with large-scale, low-resolution data, such as traffic counts and mobile phone network data. The aim is to realistically capture behaviour while remaining applicable to national-scale networks. A key expected outcome of the project is a demand estimation model for the Danish national transport model, the Green Mobility Model (GMM). Collaboration with the Danish Road Directorate (Vejdirektoratet) is therefore anticipated, to ensure real-life deployment.

The overall focus of this project is to develop scalable, behaviourally realistic methods for estimating travel demand on national-scale transport networks. You are expected to work closely with a PhD student at IPP and with the Danish Road Directorate. Your primary tasks will be to:

• Analyse and extract behavioural information from the Danish National Travel Survey.

• Build and validate a demand estimation model for the Green Mobility Model.
• Publish and present your results in international journals and conferences.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in probabilistic inversion of seismic data for mapping submerged landscapes and archaeological potential
jobs.description:
The Department of Geoscience, Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a postdoctoral position in probabilistic inversion of seismic data, with the aim of identifying submerged landscapes and locations of archaeological potential. We are searching for a motivated and engaged researcher with experience in inversion to be part of our research team studying late Quaternary and Holocene processes and landscape evolution.

The postdoctoral position is a fixed-term full-time position for 1 year.

The postdoctoral work will be part of the international ERC Synergy Grant project SUBNORDICA, where scientists in the fields of geology, geophysics, and archaeology work together to develop methodologies for recreating submerged landscapes and human settlement in NW Europe, and for finding submerged Stone Age settlements in deeper water settings such as the North Sea. SUBNORDICA also uses machine-learning routines to identify, from existing and new data, targets of archaeological potential for more detailed investigation. The research team at the department is leading a work package focused on the eastern North Sea region. Other members in the team work on geophysical imaging methods, sea level modelling, and palaeolandscape mapping to generate palaeotopography and palaeocoastlines using both legacy and newly acquired data.

Job description
The postdoctoral position is focused on probabilistic inversion of seismic data to estimate subsurface properties that can be linked directly to the location of submerged settlements – a key example being the presence of peat, which marks former dry land.

Specific tasks will be to:

• Develop probabilistic inversion workflows for high-resolution subbottom profiles and multichannel seismic data from the North Sea, constrained by sediment core observations
• Map peat and other landscape types relevant for archaeology, and use the results together with machine-learning routines to identify targets of archaeological potential
• Provide input and constraints for predictive modelling workflows carried out at partner institutions
The postdoctoral researcher will be working closely together with post docs and senior staff in the research team at the department, as well as with the international partners in the SUBNORDICA project. Close collaboration is expected particularly with partners focused on predictive modelling for archaeology. The position provides opportunities for offshore field work and participation in joint research expeditions in the North Sea and Baltic Sea. It is also expected that the postdoc will take an active part in various research team activities and contribute to supervision and teaching of (under-) graduate students in the team.

Facilities
Laboratory facilities at the Department of Geoscience will be available for the position. This includes the acquisition, processing and interpretation facilities at SeisLab Aarhus for both multi- and single channel marine seismic and acoustic data, and an advanced sediment core laboratory.

Qualifications
The qualified applicant will have a PhD degree in geoscience, geophysics or related fields. Candidates should preferably have a background within probabilistic inversion and uncertainty quantification and/or machine learning. Experience with seismic data, including reflection seismic and hydroacoustic data, is beneficial, as is experience with linking seismic data to physical or lithological properties. Experience with the shallow subsurface of the North Sea or other similar settings, including sediment cores and marine geoarchaeology, is further beneficial but not required.
